name: manual_0f93fd
claim: A bash script that runs set -u must length-guard EVERY array expansion, because macOS stock bash 3.2 treats an empty-array expansion of the form ${arr[@]} as an unbound-variable error rather than an empty expansion. Canonical idiom: [[ ${#arr[@]} -gt 0 ]] && cmd+=("${arr[@]}"). This is the THIRD recurrence of the same defect class (after commit_clean_test.sh verify_args and a profiling wrapper), so treat it as a systemic pattern: when fixing one instance, scan every set -u script in the repo with a single regex for unguarded += expansions and fix all confirmed instances, then prove the fix against a stubbed dependency that leaves the array empty.

decisions.notes: CodeRabbit review 5325082254 comment 4110603558 on Perpetua-Tools PR 400. The prior claim taught cmd+=(arr-elements), which appends the literal arr-elements. The length-guarded idiom expands the array: cmd+=("${arr[@]}"). lesson_0c7355deb939 is superseded; LESSONS.md is re-rendered from the new source record.
